newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq denies asked UN to postpone oil sale start.
newsitem.headline: Iraq denies asked UN to postpone oil sale start.

text.p: Iraq on Wednesday denied it had requested of the United Nations postponement of the start of the second phase of its oil-for-food exchange until a new aid distribution plan is in place.

"Some of the news carried by (internationa) media, which stated Iraq had asked for a postponement of the new phase of the oil-for- food agreement, are baseless and Iraq... will stick to the same procedures and measures set in the first six months (of the plan)," Iraqi newspapers quoted a foreign ministry spokesman saying.
Iraq submitted its aid distribution plan to the U.N. in New York 10 days ago and said it would not start oil exports under the deal until the U.N. approves the plan.
The U.N. said on Tuesday it was optimistic that the new aid plan could be approved this week.

Under the terms of the deal Iraq is allowed to sell up to $2 billion worth of oil every 180 days in two 90-day instalment to buy food and medicine to help offset the effects of sanctions in place since its 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
The exchange was renewed for a second six-month period beginning on June 8.

Reports from the U.N. in New York said Iraq had been hoping the latest six-month period would not start until its distribution plan had been cleared by the United Nations. The Security Council insists the clock began ticking on June 8.
This means Iraq has only until September 5 to sell the first $1 billion worth of oil allowed during each 90-day period.
Iraq's foreign ministry spokesman on Wednesday also urged U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan to speed up the approval of the aid distribution plan.
"The government of the republic of Iraq hopes the United Nations Secretary-General will approve the plan as soon as possible," the papers quoted the foreign ministry spokesman saying.

"Iraq's UN mission submitted on July 21, 1997 the new procurement and distribution plan to the (U.N.) secretary-general. The mission also handed supplements which contains list of (urgent needs) items on July 28, 1997," the spokesman said.
"The (U.N.) approval will allow (Iraq's) ministries and offices concerned to conclude contracts (with foreign companies) to purchase food, medicine and other essential needs included in the list."
